name: Withering-Chorus

civilization.name: Vaelori Choirs
civilization.notes: A culture of resonance-singers whose cities are grown from harmonizing flora; a fungal blight called the Gray Mote is killing the song-plants faster than the Vaelori can adapt.

specific_features: Quarantine zone sealing the southern continent
description: Withering-Chorus turns slowly beneath a pale amber sun, its highlands wrapped in forests of chime-trees that once rang together for hundreds of kilometers when the wind rose. Now whole valleys stand mute, their crystalline foliage gone gray and papery, and the silence spreads along the rift valleys like frost. At dusk the bioluminescent seas still glow, but the light comes in ragged pulses where it used to roll in unbroken waves.

Visitors describe the quiet as physical, a pressure behind the ears where birdsong and plant-song used to overlap. In the living groves the air tastes faintly of copper and honey, and every footstep triggers soft chords from the root-mats. After nightfall, survivors in the terraced cities keep small gardens alive with humidifiers and hymns, singing to seedlings the way others might pray.

The Vaelori were entering their industrial age when the Gray Mote appeared, first recorded in the pollen archives as a single contaminated shipment between continents. Within a generation it had crossed the quarantine lines drawn around the southern lands, which remain sealed under white perimeter pylons to this day. Off-world xenologists pay dearly for samples of the resistant strains, and no one has explained why the blight pauses, sometimes for years, before resuming its advance.

The Choirs are dying, but they are not helpless; their last great conservatory vault holds ten thousand seed-strains and a waiting list of worlds willing to host them. Smugglers risk the quarantine zones for blight-resistant heartwood worth fortunes, and worse things than fungus have been seen moving through the silent valleys at night. Whoever reaches the conservatory next will decide whether this world's music ends, migrates, or changes forever.
